sections.heading: A Headshot You're Proud to Put Everywhere
sections.imageAlt: Smiling woman photographed against a brick wall.
paragraphs: Your headshot shows up before you do — on LinkedIn, your company's team page, the conference program, the "About" page someone checks before they ever call you. It deserves better than a cropped vacation photo or that stiff picture from three jobs ago.
My headshots are warm and genuinely you: professional enough for the boardroom, human enough that people feel like they've already met you.

sections.heading: Yes — Even If You Hate Having Your Picture Taken
sections.scriptLine: You're not — you've just never been guided.
sections.imageAlt: Environmental portrait of a person in a light jacket against corrugated metal.
sections.secondaryImageAlt: Warm outdoor portrait of a person among garden flowers.
paragraphs: If your first thought is, "Just so you know, I'm terrible at this," you are not alone. You're not — you've just never been guided.

I'll direct you through the whole session: where to angle your shoulders, what to do with your hands, when to take a deep breath in through your nose and out through your mouth. Between prompts, the real expressions happen — and those are the frames you'll choose. The goal is a portrait that feels composed, confident and recognizably you.

sections.heading: How a Headshot Session Works
sections.intro: Headshot sessions are focused on purpose: a clear plan, calm direction and a concise set of images built for where you'll use them.
sections.imageAlt: Lisa Weiss reviewing photographs on the back of her camera during a portrait session.

items.heading: We plan quickly.
paragraphs: Where the headshot will live (LinkedIn? website? press?), what to wear, and the impression you want to give.

items.heading: We shoot.
paragraphs: Natural light, guided posing and enough backdrop or location variety to give you useful options without turning the session into an all-day production.

items.heading: You choose.
paragraphs: You'll see a gallery of edited images — true-to-you retouching that keeps you looking like yourself, on a very good day.

sections.heading: Headshots for Teams

items.imageAlt: Smiling woman photographed against a brick wall.
Person in a dark suit photographed on a modern staircase.

paragraphs: Headshots for a team start with a shared plan for location, light and framing, then give each person the same calm direction. Tell me your headcount and where the portraits need to live, and I'll recommend the right setup.
Building a full brand image library instead?

sections.heading: Headshot Questions
sections.imageAlt: Warm outdoor portrait of a person among garden flowers.

items.heading: What should I wear for a headshot?
paragraphs: Solid colors near your face photograph best; avoid busy patterns and large logos. We'll talk it through before your session — bring two or three options and I'll help you choose.

items.heading: How long does a headshot session take?
paragraphs: Timing depends on how many final looks you need, how many people are being photographed and whether we are changing locations or setups. Share the scope in your inquiry and I'll recommend a practical schedule.

items.heading: Headshot or branding session — which do I need?
paragraphs: If you need one great portrait, a headshot. If you need a library of images of you, your work and your space, branding.

items.heading: Do you retouch headshots?
paragraphs: Gently. I'll take care of the temporary things — a blemish, a stray hair — and leave you looking like you. No plastic skin, no stranger's face.

finalCta.heading: Let's Update That Profile Photo
paragraphs: Tell me where your headshot needs to work and when you need it.
